intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene (137190) on chromosome 4p12.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Despite lack of association with epilepsy syndromes, our results suggest GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a heterozygous de novo GABRB1 mutation in one IS patient and functional impairment, but only proposes GABRB1 as a candidate epilepsy gene; it does not establish causation of a named DEE45 disorder.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 gene is located on chromosome 4p12.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene discussed in the paper; the paper itself does not give the location.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is a severe neurologic disorder in which seizures begin in infancy, including infantile spasms, and are accompanied by impaired psychomotor development and intellectual disability. The disorder results from de novo heterozygous mutation in GABRB1, which encodes the beta-1 subunit of the GABA-A receptor.

checks.claim: DEE45 is a severe neurologic disorder in which seizures begin in infancy.
checks.explanation: Seizures in the GABRB1 patient began at 4 months, and EIMFS is described as a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy that starts in infancy.

checks.claim: Seizures in DEE45 include infantile spasms.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: The GABRB1 patient had infantile spasms (IS).

checks.claim: Seizures in DEE45 are accompanied by impaired psychomotor development.
checks.evidence_quote: While all patients showed developmental slowing at the time of refractory migrating focal seizures
checks.explanation: All patients, including the GABRB1 case, showed developmental slowing, and the table lists the GABRB1 patient with profound or severe impairment.

checks.claim: Seizures in DEE45 are accompanied by intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: The table lists the GABRB1 patient with profound-severe impairment, which the paper equates with severe to profound ID across the cohort. However, the text never specifically describes intellectual disability in this patient.

checks.claim: DEE45 results from de novo heterozygous mutation in GABRB1.
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations, we also studied α1β1,3γ2L receptors containing these mutations in the in vitro het expression condition.
checks.explanation: The paper states that the GABRB1 mutation was de novo and heterozygous.

checks.claim: GABRB1 encodes the beta-1 subunit of the GABA-A receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: 1 in the β1 subunit gene GABRB1
checks.explanation: GABRB1 is the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene.

paragraphs.text: The Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project (2013) carried out exome sequencing of patients with infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and their unaffected parents. One of these patients had seizures that began in infancy, along with developmental delay.

checks.claim: The Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project carried out exome sequencing of patients with infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and their unaffected parents.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we report a screen for de novo mutations in patients with two classical epileptic encephalopathies: infantile spasms (n = 149) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (n = 115). We sequenced the exomes of 264 probands, and their parents
checks.explanation: Unaffected parents are also stated: 'both biological parents had to have no past medical history of seizures'.

checks.claim: One patient in the Epi4K exome sequencing study (the GABRB1 DEE45 patient) had seizures that began in infancy.
checks.explanation: The main text gives no individual clinical details, including onset age, for the GABRB1 patient.

checks.claim: One patient in the Epi4K exome sequencing study (the GABRB1 DEE45 patient) had developmental delay.
checks.explanation: The paper does not describe developmental delay in the GABRB1 patient.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous GABRB1 mutation in the reported patient arose de novo (Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project, 2013). This is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: The heterozygous GABRB1 mutation in the patient reported by the Epi4K Consortium arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: The paper reports the mutations as de novo but does not explicitly state that the GABRB1 mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The de novo occurrence of the heterozygous GABRB1 mutation in DEE45 is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.explanation: The paper does not discuss the inheritance pattern of GABRB1-related disease.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with epileptic encephalopathy, the Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project (2013) found a de novo heterozygous missense mutation in the GABRB1 gene (phe246-to-ser; F246S) using trio exome sequencing.

checks.claim: The Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project found a heterozygous missense mutation in the GABRB1 gene, F246S (phe246-to-ser), in a patient with epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: The paper reports one GABRB1 mutation in an epileptic encephalopathy patient. The specific variant (F246S), its missense type and its zygosity are not given in the supplied text; they are probably in the supplementary tables.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation in the patient with epileptic encephalopathy arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: These are among the confirmed de novo mutations found in the cohort. The variant identity itself is not stated.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation was identified by trio exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing of 264 trios (Additional Methods) identified 439 putative de novo mutations.
checks.explanation: The mutations were identified by trio exome sequencing.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) studied the function of de novo GABRB mutations associated with epileptic encephalopathy, including the GABRB1 mutation, by expressing them in heterologous cells. The mutations altered GABA-A receptor function.

checks.claim: Janve et al. (2016) studied the function of de novo GABRB mutations associated with epileptic encephalopathy, including the GABRB1 mutation, by expressing them in heterologous cells.
checks.evidence_quote: GABAA receptor α1 and γ2L subunits were coexpressed with wild-type and/or mutant β3 or β1 subunits in HEK 293T cells.
checks.explanation: The mutations were studied by expression in HEK293T heterologous cells.

checks.claim: The de novo GABRB mutations associated with epileptic encephalopathy, including the GABRB1 mutation, altered GABA-A receptor function when expressed in heterologous cells.
checks.evidence_quote: All 5 de novo GABRB mutations impaired GABAA receptor function by rearranging conserved structural domains, supporting their role in EEs.
checks.explanation: All five mutations, including the GABRB1 mutation, impaired receptor function.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with epileptic encephalopathy, the Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project (2013) found a de novo heterozygous phe246-to-ser (F246S) mutation in the GABRB1 gene using trio exome sequencing. Janve et al. (2016) studied the mutation in vitro and found that it impaired GABA-A receptor function.

checks.claim: The Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project found a heterozygous F246S (phe246-to-ser) mutation in the GABRB1 gene in a patient with epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: F246S in GABRB1 was found in an IS (epileptic encephalopathy) patient; elsewhere the paper states the patients were heterozygous.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation in the patient with epileptic encephalopathy arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: The Epi4K Consortium recently identified 4 de novo mutations in the γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA ) receptor β3 subunit gene GABRB3 and 1 in the β1 subunit gene GABRB1
checks.explanation: The GABRB1 mutation is described as de novo.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation was identified by trio exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: By analysis of triads with LGS and IS, three GABRB3 mutations were associated with LGS and one GABRB1 and one GABRB3 mutations were associated with IS
checks.explanation: Trio analysis is mentioned, but exome sequencing is not explicitly stated.

checks.claim: Janve et al. (2016) found in vitro that the GABRB1 F246S mutation impaired GABA-A receptor function.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast, IS-associated GABRB3(N110D) and GABRB1(F246S) mutations at β- subunit interfaces produced minor changes in whole cell current peak amplitude but altered current deactivation by decreasing or increasing single channel burst duration, respectively.
checks.explanation: In vitro, F246S altered receptor kinetics and caused spontaneous openings, i.e., it impaired receptor function.

references.label: Janve et al. (2016)
references.citation: Janve VS, Hernandez CC, Verdier KM, Hu N, Macdonald RL. Epileptic encephalopathy de novo GABRB mutations impair γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor function. Ann Neurol 79: 806-825, 2016. [PubMed: 26950270]
